To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a staggered-grid finite-difference scheme can be developed to model Biot’s equations in the seismic frequency band and (2) the stability of the method is governed by the usual Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) condition, which is independent of the fluid viscosity.

the finite difference scheme for Biot’s equations presented in this work is unconditionally stable and convergent for all porous materials with the usual Courant stability condition, even in the presence of Biot slow waves.
the stability condition for Biot’s equations is the Courant stability criterion for purely elastic waves and the accuracy is comparable to the finite-difference method for elastic wave propagation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a finite difference method for solving the equations of linear poroelasticity at low frequencies.
the development of an efficient, stable, and accurate finite difference model of poroelastic wave propagation at seismic frequencies, and we have achieved this goal.
the development and validation of a finite-difference model for simulating the seismic response of porous rock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite difference scheme described in this paper is stable, accurate, and computationally efficient for solving Biot's equations in the low-frequency limit.

, at seismic frequencies, a staggered-grid explicit time-stepping finite difference scheme for Biot’s equations is stable, unconditionally for the fast waves (elastic waves), and unconditionally stable for the slow waves (diffusive pressure waves) if the time step is less than a certain critical value that depends on the material properties of the porous rock.
the finite difference scheme presented is stable for all Courant numbers less than or equal to one and is accurate to the fourth order for all wave types and for all porous material properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a staggered-grid finite-difference scheme is a viable and efficient way to solve the equations of poro-elasticity for seismic frequencies.
the method presented is a robust numerical technique for simulating the propagation of seismic waves through a poroelastic medium.
the method presented here can be used to model seismic waves in porous materials with confidence in the results.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a wide range of material properties typical of porous rock, explicit finite difference modeling of BIoT’s equations of poromechanics can be performed at seismic frequencies with a time step that is governed by the Courant condition, as if the problem were purely elastic.
the finite difference equations presented here can be used with confidence to solve Biot’s equations in a wide range of situations.
a finite difference method that is stable and accurate for the elastic wave equation can also be used to model poroelasticity at low frequencies.
